questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: A synthetic polymer blend is prepared by mixing equimolar amounts of two monodisperse polymer fractions having molecular masses $M_1 = 20{,}000\text{ g/mol}$ and $M_2 = 60{,}000\text{ g/mol}$. What is the polydispersity index ($\text{PDI} = \bar{M}_w / \bar{M}_n$) of this blend?
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Calculate the number-average molecular weight ($\bar{M}_n$). For an equimolar blend ($N_1 = N_2 = 1$), substituting into the formula gives $\bar{M}_n = \frac{N_1 M_1 + N_2 M_2}{N_1 + N_2} = \frac{20{,}000 + 60{,}000}{2} = 40{,}000\text{ g/mol}$.
Step 2: Calculate the weight-average molecular weight ($\bar{M}_w$). Substituting gives $\bar{M}_w = \frac{N_1 M_1^2 + N_2 M_2^2}{N_1 M_1 + N_2 M_2} = \frac{1(20{,}000)^2 + 1(60{,}000)^2}{20{,}000 + 60{,}000} = \frac{4.0\times 10^8 + 3.6\times 10^9}{80{,}000} = \frac{4.0\times 10^9}{80{,}000} = 50{,}000\text{ g/mol}$.
Step 3: Therefore, determine the polydispersity index: $\text{PDI} = \frac{\bar{M}_w}{\bar{M}_n} = \frac{50{,}000}{40{,}000} = 1.25$.
A value of $1.50$ results from mistakenly inverting the ratio or computing an unweighted arithmetic average of mass ratios. A value of $1.33$ arises from confusing number and weight fractions, and $1.10$ reflects an arithmetic averaging error.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: A sample of poly(methyl methacrylate) (PMMA) synthesized by addition polymerization has a number-average molecular weight $\bar{M}_n = 150{,}000\text{ g/mol}$. Given the structure of the methyl methacrylate monomer $\text{CH}_2=\text{C}(\text{CH}_3)\text{COOCH}_3$, calculate the number-average degree of polymerization $\bar{X}_n$ of this polymer sample.
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Determine the molecular formula and molar mass of the monomer. Methyl methacrylate is $\text{CH}_2=\text{C}(\text{CH}_3)\text{COOCH}_3$, giving molecular formula $\text{C}_5\text{H}_8\text{O}_2$. Molar mass $M_0 = (5\times 12) + (8\times 1) + (2\times 16) = 60 + 8 + 32 = 100\text{ g/mol}$.
Step 2: Since PMMA is an addition polymer, the repeating unit has the exact same formula and molar mass as the monomer ($M_0 = 100\text{ g/mol}$).
Step 3: Therefore, applying the definition of degree of polymerization, substituting known values gives $\bar{X}_n = \frac{\bar{M}_n}{M_0} = \frac{150{,}000}{100} = 1500$.
A value of $1200$ results from assuming methyl acrylate instead of methyl methacrylate ($M_0 = 86\text{ g/mol}$). A value of $1800$ comes from mistakenly subtracting water as if it were a condensation polymer.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: In the synthesis of Nylon 6,6, equimolar quantities of hexamethylenediamine (molar mass $116\text{ g/mol}$) and adipic acid (molar mass $146\text{ g/mol}$) undergo polycondensation. For every repeat unit $-[\text{NH}-(\text{CH}_2)_6-\text{NH}-\text{CO}-(\text{CH}_2)_4-\text{CO}]-$ formed in a high-molecular-weight chain, two molecules of water (molar mass $18\text{ g/mol}$) are eliminated. What percentage of the initial total monomer mass is lost as water?
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Compute the combined mass of the reacting stoichiometric monomer pair: $M_{\text{reactants}} = M_{\text{diamine}} + M_{\text{diacid}} = 116 + 146 = 262\text{ g/mol}$.
Step 2: Identify the water molecules eliminated per repeat unit. The formation of each repeating unit $-[\text{NH}-(\text{CH}_2)_6-\text{NH}-\text{CO}-(\text{CH}_2)_4-\text{CO}]-$ creates two amide bonds, eliminating two $\text{H}_2\text{O}$ molecules: $M_{\text{water}} = 2\times 18 = 36\text{ g/mol}$.
Step 3: Therefore, substituting into the mass fraction formula, applying division yields $\text{Percentage loss} = \frac{36}{262} \times 100\% = 13.74\% \approx 13.7\%$.
A value of $6.9\%$ results from assuming only one molecule of water is eliminated per repeat unit. A value of $18.2\%$ results from calculating water loss relative only to the repeat unit mass ($36/198$) or neglecting one monomer component.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: A polydisperse sample of polystyrene consists of $2.0\text{ moles}$ of polymer molecules with molecular weight $M_1 = 30{,}000\text{ g/mol}$ and $3.0\text{ moles}$ of polymer molecules with molecular weight $M_2 = 80{,}000\text{ g/mol}$. What is the number-average molecular weight $\bar{M}_n$ of this combined polymer sample?
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Determine the total mass of the polymer mixture: $W_{\text{total}} = N_1 M_1 + N_2 M_2 = (2.0\text{ mol} \times 30{,}000\text{ g/mol}) + (3.0\text{ mol} \times 80{,}000\text{ g/mol}) = 60{,}000 + 240{,}000 = 300{,}000\text{ g}$.
Step 2: Find the total number of moles of chains: $N_{\text{total}} = N_1 + N_2 = 2.0 + 3.0 = 5.0\text{ mol}$.
Step 3: Therefore, substituting into the definition of number-average molecular weight, solving yields $\bar{M}_n = \frac{W_{\text{total}}}{N_{\text{total}}} = \frac{300{,}000}{5.0} = 60{,}000\text{ g/mol}$.
A value of $55{,}000\text{ g/mol}$ is the simple unweighted arithmetic mean $\frac{30{,}000 + 80{,}000}{2}$, which overlooks the higher molar abundance of the heavier fraction. A value of $65{,}000\text{ g/mol}$ or $50{,}000\text{ g/mol}$ arises from inverting the molar weighting factors.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: A $4.00\text{ g}$ sample of a linear polyester having carboxy terminal groups ($-\text{COOH}$) at both ends of every polymer chain is dissolved in a solvent and titrated with standardized $0.050\text{ M NaOH}_{\text{(aq)}}$. The titration requires exactly $20.0\text{ mL}$ of the $\text{NaOH}$ solution to reach the phenolphthalein end point. Determine the number-average molecular weight $\bar{M}_n$ of the polyester in $\text{g/mol}$, and report the value of $\frac{\bar{M}_n}{1000}$ as an integer.
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Calculate the total moles of hydroxide ions neutralized in the titration: $n_{\text{OH}^-} = M \times V = 0.050\text{ mol/L} \times 0.0200\text{ L} = 1.00\times 10^{-3}\text{ mol}$.
Step 2: Relate the moles of titrant to the moles of polymer molecules. Because each linear polyester chain is telechelic with two terminal carboxy groups (difunctional acid), substituting into stoichiometry gives $n_{\text{polymer}} = \frac{n_{\text{OH}^-}}{2} = \frac{1.00\times 10^{-3}}{2} = 5.00\times 10^{-4}\text{ mol}$.
Step 3: Applying definition of molar mass, solving yields $\bar{M}_n = \frac{\text{mass}}{n_{\text{polymer}}} = \frac{4.00\text{ g}}{5.00\times 10^{-4}\text{ mol}} = 8000\text{ g/mol}$.
Step 4: Therefore, dividing by $1000$ yields $\frac{8000}{1000} = 8$. Forgetting that each linear chain has two terminal groups yields an erroneous $\bar{M}_n = 4000\text{ g/mol}$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: A polymeric material is formulated by blending two monodisperse polymer samples in equal mass fractions ($50\%$ each by weight). Sample 1 has a molecular weight of $M_1 = 40{,}000\text{ g/mol}$ and Sample 2 has a molecular weight of $M_2 = 120{,}000\text{ g/mol}$. What is the weight-average molecular weight $\bar{M}_w$ of this blend?
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Recall the definition of weight-average molecular weight in terms of weight fractions: $\bar{M}_w = \sum w_i M_i$, where $w_i = \frac{m_i}{\sum m_i}$ is the weight fraction of species $i$.
Step 2: Substitute the given weight fractions ($w_1 = 0.50$ and $w_2 = 0.50$): $\bar{M}_w = (0.50 \times 40{,}000\text{ g/mol}) + (0.50 \times 120{,}000\text{ g/mol}) = 20{,}000 + 60{,}000 = 80{,}000\text{ g/mol}$.
Step 3: Therefore, solving directly yields $\bar{M}_w = 80{,}000\text{ g/mol}$.
A value of $60{,}000\text{ g/mol}$ represents the number-average molecular weight $\bar{M}_n$ of this blend: $\bar{M}_n = \frac{1}{\sum (w_i/M_i)} = \frac{1}{\frac{0.5}{40{,}000} + \frac{0.5}{120{,}000}} = 60{,}000\text{ g/mol}$. Confusing weight-average with number-average leads to the distractor $60{,}000\text{ g/mol}$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Polyethylene terephthalate (PET, Dacron) is prepared by the step-growth condensation of terephthalic acid ($p-\text{HOOC}-\text{C}_6\text{H}_4-\text{COOH}$) and ethylene glycol ($\text{HO}-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_2-\text{OH}$). A purified sample of Dacron exhibits a number-average molecular weight $\bar{M}_n = 38{,}400\text{ g/mol}$. What is the number-average degree of polymerization $\bar{X}_n$ of this polymer sample?
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Determine the chemical formula of the constitutional repeating unit of Dacron. Condensation of one terephthalic acid molecule ($\text{C}_8\text{H}_6\text{O}_4$) and one ethylene glycol molecule ($\text{C}_2\text{H}_6\text{O}_2$) eliminates two water molecules ($2\times \text{H}_2\text{O} = \text{H}_4\text{O}_2$), yielding repeating unit $-[\text{O}-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_2-\text{O}-\text{CO}-\text{C}_6\text{H}_4-\text{CO}]-$ with molecular formula $\text{C}_{10}\text{H}_8\text{O}_4$.
Step 2: Calculate the repeat unit molecular weight: substituting atomic weights gives $M_0 = (10\times 12) + (8\times 1) + (4\times 16) = 120 + 8 + 64 = 192\text{ g/mol}$.
Step 3: Therefore, applying definition of degree of polymerization, solving yields $\bar{X}_n = \frac{\bar{M}_n}{M_0} = \frac{38{,}400}{192} = 200$.
A value of $150$ arises from mistakenly including the uneliminated water molecules ($M_0 = 228\text{ g/mol}$), while $250$ arises from using the terephthalate fragment mass alone ($M_0 = 148\text{ g/mol}$).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: A batch of polyvinyl chloride (PVC) is produced by free-radical addition polymerization of vinyl chloride ($\text{CH}_2=\text{CHCl}$, atomic weights: $\text{C} = 12.0$, $\text{H} = 1.0$, $\text{Cl} = 35.5\text{ g/mol}$). If a manufacturing process consumes $1.00\text{ kg}$ of pure PVC resin, what is the exact total mass of chlorine element contained in this resin?
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Compute the molar mass of the vinyl chloride monomer and repeating unit: substituting atomic masses yields $M_0 = (2 \times 12.0) + (3 \times 1.0) + 35.5 = 24.0 + 3.0 + 35.5 = 62.5\text{ g/mol}$.
Step 2: Determine the mass fraction of chlorine in each repeating unit $-[\text{CH}_2-\text{CHCl}]-$: substituting gives $w_{\text{Cl}} = \frac{35.5}{62.5} = 0.568$ (or $56.8\%$ by mass).
Step 3: Therefore, applying this fraction to $1.00\text{ kg} = 1000\text{ g}$ of pure PVC, solving yields $m_{\text{Cl}} = 1000\text{ g} \times 0.568 = 568\text{ g}$.
A value of $432\text{ g}$ corresponds to the hydrocarbon backbone mass ($1000 - 568\text{ g}$). A value of $355\text{ g}$ comes from assuming a molar mass of $100\text{ g/mol}$, and $625\text{ g}$ is the inverse ratio distractor.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: A synthetic polymer sample consists of three distinct monodisperse fractions: $1.0\text{ mol}$ of chains with molecular mass $10{,}000\text{ g/mol}$, $2.0\text{ mol}$ of chains with molecular mass $20{,}000\text{ g/mol}$, and $1.0\text{ mol}$ of chains with molecular mass $30{,}000\text{ g/mol}$. If the polydispersity index of this polymer sample is denoted by $\text{PDI} = \frac{\bar{M}_w}{\bar{M}_n}$, calculate the value of $8 \times \text{PDI}$.
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Compute total moles and number-average molecular weight: $\sum N_i = 1.0 + 2.0 + 1.0 = 4.0\text{ mol}$. Total mass $\sum N_i M_i = 1(10{,}000) + 2(20{,}000) + 1(30{,}000) = 80{,}000\text{ g}$. Hence $\bar{M}_n = \frac{80{,}000}{4.0} = 20{,}000\text{ g/mol}$.
Step 2: Compute weight-average molecular weight: $\sum N_i M_i^2 = 1(10{,}000)^2 + 2(20{,}000)^2 + 1(30{,}000)^2 = 1.0\times 10^8 + 8.0\times 10^8 + 9.0\times 10^8 = 1.8\times 10^9\text{ g}^2/\text{mol}$. Thus substituting into $\bar{M}_w$ gives $\bar{M}_w = \frac{1.8\times 10^9}{80{,}000} = 22{,}500\text{ g/mol}$.
Step 3: Calculate $\text{PDI} = \frac{\bar{M}_w}{\bar{M}_n} = \frac{22{,}500}{20{,}000} = 1.125 = \frac{9}{8}$.
Step 4: Therefore, multiplying by $8$ yields $8 \times 1.125 = 9$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: A sample of $5.30\text{ g}$ of polyacrylonitrile (PAN, repeating unit derived from $\text{CH}_2=\text{CH}-\text{CN}$, atomic masses: $\text{C}=12$, $\text{H}=1$, $\text{N}=14\text{ g/mol}$) is subjected to complete Kjeldahl digestion. All nitrogen is quantitatively converted into ammonia ($\text{NH}_3$) and distilled into excess acid. What volume of $1.00\text{ M HCl}_{\text{(aq)}}$ is required to neutralize the ammonia generated from this sample?
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Calculate the molar mass of the acrylonitrile repeat unit $-[\text{CH}_2-\text{CH(CN)}]-$: $M_0 = (3\times 12) + (3\times 1) + 14 = 36 + 3 + 14 = 53\text{ g/mol}$.
Step 2: Determine the moles of repeating units present in $5.30\text{ g}$ of polymer: substituting gives $n = \frac{5.30\text{ g}}{53\text{ g/mol}} = 0.100\text{ mol}$.
Step 3: Each unit contains one nitrogen atom, yielding $0.100\text{ mol}$ of $\text{NH}_3$ upon complete digestion.
Step 4: Therefore, using $1:1$ stoichiometry between $\text{NH}_3$ and $\text{HCl}$, applying $V = \frac{n}{M}$ gives $V = \frac{0.100\text{ mol}}{1.00\text{ mol/L}} = 0.100\text{ L} = 100\text{ mL}$.
A value of $53\text{ mL}$ comes from confusing molar mass with volume, while $50\text{ mL}$ or $200\text{ mL}$ results from an incorrect assumed stoichiometric ratio.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: A solution prepared by dissolving $2.50\text{ g}$ of polystyrene in toluene to a final volume of $250\text{ mL}$ exerts an osmotic pressure of $2.49\times 10^{-3}\text{ bar}$ at $300\text{ K}$. Assuming ideal solution behavior with the universal gas constant $R = 0.08314\text{ L bar K}^{-1}\text{mol}^{-1}$, what is the number-average molecular weight $\bar{M}_n$ of this polystyrene sample?
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Express the mass concentration of the polymer solution: $C = \frac{\text{mass}}{V} = \frac{2.50\text{ g}}{0.250\text{ L}} = 10.0\text{ g/L}$.
Step 2: Apply the van 't Hoff osmotic pressure relation for polymers: $\Pi = \frac{C}{\bar{M}_n} R T$, which rearranges to $\bar{M}_n = \frac{C R T}{\Pi}$.
Step 3: Substitute the known values: $\bar{M}_n = \frac{10.0\text{ g/L} \times 0.08314\text{ L bar K}^{-1}\text{mol}^{-1} \times 300\text{ K}}{2.49\times 10^{-3}\text{ bar}} = \frac{249.42}{2.49\times 10^{-3}} = 100{,}168\text{ g/mol} \approx 100{,}000\text{ g/mol}$.
Step 4: Therefore, solving directly confirms $\bar{M}_n = 100{,}000\text{ g/mol}$.
A value of $50{,}000\text{ g/mol}$ or $200{,}000\text{ g/mol}$ results from volume conversion errors (using $250\text{ L}$ or neglecting conversion of $\text{mL}$ to $\text{L}$) or misapplying factor of 2.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Tetrafluoroethylene ($\text{CF}_2=\text{CF}_2$, molar mass $100\text{ g/mol}$) is polymerized to form Teflon (polytetrafluoroethylene, PTFE). If $500\text{ g}$ of monomer is subjected to polymerization achieving a $92\%$ fractional conversion to polymer, and the resulting PTFE has a number-average degree of polymerization $\bar{X}_n = 2500$, how many moles of PTFE polymer chains are produced?
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Calculate the mass of monomer converted into polymer: $m_{\text{polymer}} = 500\text{ g} \times 0.92 = 460\text{ g}$.
Step 2: Determine the number-average molecular weight of the PTFE chains: since Teflon is an addition polymer, the repeat unit mass equals the monomer mass ($100\text{ g/mol}$). Substituting gives $\bar{M}_n = \bar{X}_n \times M_0 = 2500 \times 100\text{ g/mol} = 250{,}000\text{ g/mol}$.
Step 3: Therefore, applying $n_{\text{chains}} = \frac{m_{\text{polymer}}}{\bar{M}_n}$, solving yields $n_{\text{chains}} = \frac{460\text{ g}}{250{,}000\text{ g/mol}} = 1.84\times 10^{-3}\text{ mol}$.
A value of $2.00\times 10^{-3}\text{ mol}$ ignores the $92\%$ conversion efficiency ($500/250{,}000$). A value of $3.68\times 10^{-3}\text{ mol}$ results from an extra factor of 2, and $4.60\times 10^{-3}\text{ mol}$ arises from dividing total moles of monomer by 1000.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Poly($\beta$-hydroxybutyrate-co-$\beta$-hydroxyvalerate) (PHBV) is a biodegradable polyester copolymer prepared from 3-hydroxybutanoic acid ($\text{C}_4\text{H}_8\text{O}_3$, molar mass $104\text{ g/mol}$) and 3-hydroxypentanoic acid ($\text{C}_5\text{H}_{10}\text{O}_3$, molar mass $118\text{ g/mol}$). In a specific copolymer formulation, the monomer mole ratio of 3-hydroxybutanoic acid to 3-hydroxypentanoic acid is $3:1$. During step-growth condensation, each ester linkage formation eliminates one molecule of $\text{H}_2\text{O}$ ($18\text{ g/mol}$). What is the average molar mass of a repeating unit in this PHBV copolymer?
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Find the molar masses of the two constitutional repeating units after eliminating water: for the 3-hydroxybutanoate unit, $M_1 = 104 - 18 = 86\text{ g/mol}$; for the 3-hydroxypentanoate unit, $M_2 = 118 - 18 = 100\text{ g/mol}$.
Step 2: Determine the mole fractions corresponding to the $3:1$ ratio: $x_1 = \frac{3}{4} = 0.75$ and $x_2 = \frac{1}{4} = 0.25$.
Step 3: Therefore, substituting into the weighted average formula, solving yields $M_{\text{avg}} = (0.75 \times 86) + (0.25 \times 100) = 64.5 + 25.0 = 89.5\text{ g/mol}$.
A value of $107.5\text{ g/mol}$ (or $102.5\text{ g/mol}$) results from failing to subtract water of condensation from the monomer masses. A value of $93.0\text{ g/mol}$ corresponds to an equimolar ($1:1$) blend $\frac{86 + 100}{2}$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Glyptal resin is synthesized by the step-growth condensation of phthalic anhydride with glycerol. In the reaction mixture, phthalic anhydride acts as a difunctional carboxylic acid precursor ($f_1 = 2$), while glycerol (propane-1,2,3-triol) acts as a trifunctional polyol ($f_2 = 3$). If an equimolar reaction mixture containing $1.0\text{ mol}$ of phthalic anhydride and $1.0\text{ mol}$ of glycerol is polymerized, what is the average functionality $f_{\text{avg}}$ of this monomer system?
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Identify the functionality of each monomer component. Phthalic anhydride has two acyl reactive sites ($f_1 = 2$), while glycerol contains three aliphatic hydroxyl groups ($f_2 = 3$).
Step 2: Calculate total functional groups and total monomer molecules for the equimolar mixture: total functional groups $= (1.0 \times 2) + (1.0 \times 3) = 2 + 3 = 5\text{ equivalents}$. Total moles of monomers $= 1.0 + 1.0 = 2.0\text{ mol}$.
Step 3: Therefore, substituting into definition of average functionality, solving yields $f_{\text{avg}} = \frac{\text{total functional groups}}{\text{total monomer molecules}} = \frac{5}{2.0} = 2.50$.
A value of $2.33$ results from using a $2:1$ phthalic anhydride to glycerol ratio, whereas $2.00$ or $3.00$ represents single-component functionality without accounting for the co-reactant.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Caprolactam ($\text{C}_6\text{H}_{11}\text{NO}$, molar mass $113.16\text{ g/mol}$) is heated with a catalytic amount of water at $530\text{ K}$ to produce Nylon 6 via ring-opening polymerization. Because ring-opening does not eliminate any small condensation byproduct, the constitutional repeating unit $-[\text{NH}-(\text{CH}_2)_5-\text{CO}]-$ has a formula weight of $113.16\text{ g/mol}$. If a batch of purified Nylon 6 has a number-average molecular weight $\bar{M}_n = 28{,}290\text{ g/mol}$, calculate its number-average degree of polymerization $\bar{X}_n$ as an integer.
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Recall that ring-opening polymerization of caprolactam incorporates the entire monomer molecule into the linear polymer chain without eliminating water. Thus, the repeating unit molecular mass equals the monomer mass: $M_0 = 113.16\text{ g/mol}$.
Step 2: Apply the relationship between number-average molecular weight and degree of polymerization: $\bar{M}_n = \bar{X}_n \times M_0$.
Step 3: Substituting known values and solving for $\bar{X}_n$ yields $\bar{X}_n = \frac{\bar{M}_n}{M_0} = \frac{28{,}290\text{ g/mol}}{113.16\text{ g/mol}} = 250$.
Step 4: Therefore, the integer degree of polymerization is 250.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: During the thermal initiation of styrene polymerization at $80^\circ\text{C}$ using benzoyl peroxide ($(\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{COO})_2$), the initiator undergoes homolytic cleavage of the peroxide bond to yield two benzoyloxy radicals ($\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{COO}\cdot$), which can decarboxylate to phenyl radicals ($\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\cdot$). If $0.010\text{ mol}$ of benzoyl peroxide is decomposed in styrene with an initiator efficiency $f = 0.80$, how many moles of primary propagating polystyrene chains are initiated?
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Write the stoichiometric homolysis equation: $(\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{COO})_2 \to 2\,\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{COO}\cdot$. Each mole of benzoyl peroxide decomposes homolytically to yield $2\text{ moles}$ of primary free radicals.
Step 2: Calculate theoretical total moles of generated radicals: $n_{\text{radicals, theoretical}} = 2 \times 0.010\text{ mol} = 0.020\text{ mol}$.
Step 3: Account for initiator efficiency $f = 0.80$, which represents the fraction of generated radicals that successfully escape the solvent cage and initiate chain growth: $n_{\text{initiated}} = f \times n_{\text{radicals, theoretical}} = 0.80 \times 0.020\text{ mol} = 0.016\text{ mol}$.
Step 4: Therefore, substituting into the rate equation, solving yields $0.016\text{ mol}$ of initiated chains.
A value of $0.008\text{ mol}$ overlooks that each peroxide yields two initiating radicals ($0.80 \times 0.010$). A value of $0.020\text{ mol}$ assumes $100\%$ initiator efficiency ($f = 1.0$), and $0.010\text{ mol}$ ignores both the stoichiometric factor of 2 and the cage recombination efficiency.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: In the free-radical polymerization of styrene in bulk, bimolecular chain termination occurs almost exclusively by combination (coupling) of two growing macroradicals rather than by disproportionation. If steady-state kinetic measurements under specific conditions give a kinetic chain length $\nu = 650$ (where $\nu = R_p / R_t$) with negligible chain transfer, what is the resulting number-average degree of polymerization $\bar{X}_n$?
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Define kinetic chain length $
u$: it is the average number of monomer molecules consumed per active radical initiated, $
u =  rac{R_p}{R_i} =  rac{R_p}{R_t}$ at steady state.
Step 2: Relate kinetic chain length to number-average degree of polymerization $ ar{X}_n$ based on termination mode. When two growing radical chains $	ext{P}_n\cdot + 	ext{P}_m\cdot 	o 	ext{P}_{n+m}$ terminate by combination, two propagating chains combine to form a single dead polymer molecule.
Step 3: Therefore, substituting the combination condition gives $ ar{X}_n = 2
u = 2 	imes 650 = 1300$.
If termination were exclusively by disproportionation (hydrogen abstraction producing two separate dead chains), $ ar{X}_n = 
u = 650$. The value $325$ erroneously divides by 2, and $2600$ applies an unnecessary factor of 4.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: When styrene is polymerized by free-radical addition in the presence of carbon tetrachloride ($\text{CCl}_4$) as a solvent and chain-transfer agent, the growing macroradical $\text{P}_n\cdot$ abstracts a chlorine atom: $\text{P}_n\cdot + \text{CCl}_4 \to \text{P}_n-\text{Cl} + \cdot\text{CCl}_3$. The resulting trichloromethyl radical initiates a new chain: $\cdot\text{CCl}_3 + \text{M} \to \text{Cl}_3\text{C}-\text{M}\cdot$. What terminal end groups are present on a dead polystyrene chain that was initiated by $\cdot\text{CCl}_3$ and terminated by chlorine atom abstraction from $\text{CCl}_4$?
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Track the initiating step: the trichloromethyl radical $\cdot\text{CCl}_3$ adds to the first monomer unit to yield $\text{Cl}_3\text{C}-\text{CH}_2-\dot{\text{C}}\text{H}(\text{C}_6\text{H}_5)$, so the chain head contains a $-\text{CCl}_3$ terminal group.
Step 2: Track the termination step by chain transfer: the propagating macroradical $\text{Cl}_3\text{C}-(\text{C}_8\text{H}_8)_n\cdot$ abstracts a chlorine atom from another $\text{CCl}_4$ molecule: $\text{Cl}_3\text{C}-(\text{C}_8\text{H}_8)_n\cdot + \text{CCl}_4 \to \text{Cl}_3\text{C}-(\text{C}_8\text{H}_8)_n-\text{Cl} + \cdot\text{CCl}_3$.
Step 3: Therefore, the resulting dead chain is telomerized with a $-\text{CCl}_3$ group at one terminus and a $-\text{Cl}$ group at the other terminus (telechelic telomer $\text{Cl}_3\text{C}-(\text{M})_n-\text{Cl}$).
Terminal $-\text{H}$ and $-\text{OH}$ or $-\text{COOH}$ and $-\text{NH}_2$ belong to redox or condensation polymers, while $-\text{CH}_3$ and $-\text{CHCl}_2$ would require hydrogen abstraction rather than halogen abstraction.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Buna-S (styrene-butadiene rubber, SBR) is an addition copolymer produced from 1,3-butadiene ($\text{C}_4\text{H}_6$, molar mass $54.09\text{ g/mol}$) and styrene ($\text{C}_8\text{H}_8$, molar mass $104.15\text{ g/mol}$) in an exact $3:1$ molar ratio. In 1,4-addition of 1,3-butadiene, each butadiene unit retains one olefinic double bond. If $1000\text{ g}$ of pure Buna-S copolymer having this $3:1$ molar stoichiometry is selectively catalytically hydrogenated to saturate all aliphatic olefinic double bonds (leaving the aromatic phenyl rings intact), how many moles of $\text{H}_2$ gas are consumed?
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Calculate the molar mass of the four-monomer stoichiometric sequence ($3$ butadiene units $+ 1$ styrene unit): $M_{\text{block}} = (3 \times 54.09\text{ g/mol}) + (1 \times 104.15\text{ g/mol}) = 162.27 + 104.15 = 266.42\text{ g/mol}$.
Step 2: Determine the number of moles of this four-unit block in $1000\text{ g}$ of copolymer: $n_{\text{block}} = \frac{1000\text{ g}}{266.42\text{ g/mol}} = 3.7535\text{ mol}$.
Step 3: Count the reactive aliphatic double bonds per block. Each 1,4-butadiene unit retains one $-\text{CH}=\text{CH}-$ double bond, yielding 3 aliphatic double bonds per block. The phenyl ring of styrene is aromatic and resists hydrogenation under mild selective conditions.
Step 4: Therefore, substituting into stoichiometry, solving yields $n_{\text{H}_2} = 3 \times n_{\text{block}} = 3 \times 3.7535 = 11.26\text{ mol} \approx 11.3\text{ mol}$.
A value of $3.75\text{ mol}$ accounts for only 1 double bond per block, $7.50\text{ mol}$ accounts for 2 double bonds, and $15.0\text{ mol}$ mistakenly includes hydrogenation of the aromatic ring double bonds.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: An ebonite (hard rubber) sample is produced by extensive vulcanization of natural rubber (cis-1,4-polyisoprene, repeat unit formula $\text{C}_5\text{H}_8$, molar mass $68\text{ g/mol}$) with elemental sulfur (atomic mass $\text{S} = 32\text{ g/mol}$). The vulcanization process incorporates cross-links such that, on average, exactly one sulfur atom is added per isoprene repeating unit without eliminating any atoms. Calculate the mass percentage of sulfur in this vulcanized ebonite sample as an integer.
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Identify the components and molecular weights: each repeat unit of polyisoprene has formula $\text{C}_5\text{H}_8$ with molar mass $M_{\text{isoprene}} = (5\times 12) + (8\times 1) = 68\text{ g/mol}$.
Step 2: Account for incorporated sulfur: one sulfur atom of atomic mass $M_{\text{S}} = 32\text{ g/mol}$ is added per isoprene unit.
Step 3: Calculate the total combined mass of the vulcanized repeat unit: $M_{\text{total}} = 68 + 32 = 100\text{ g/mol}$.
Step 4: Therefore, applying definition of mass percentage, solving yields $\%\,\text{S} = \frac{32}{100} \times 100\% = 32\%$. The integer answer is 32.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Novolac is an initial linear condensation prepolymer prepared by reacting phenol with formaldehyde in the presence of an acid catalyst with a molar ratio of formaldehyde to phenol strictly less than 1. Mechanistically, protonated formaldehyde ($^+\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$) acts as an electrophile attacking the benzene ring of phenol. What specific structural bridges connect the phenolic aromatic rings in the linear Novolac polymer, and at which positions of the phenolic rings do these linkages occur?
options: A) Methylene bridges ($-\text{CH}_2-$) connecting ortho and para positions
B) Ether linkages ($-\text{CH}_2-\text{O}-\text{CH}_2-$) connecting meta positions exclusively
C) Direct biphenyl $\text{C}-\text{C}$ bonds connecting para positions only
D) Carbonyl bridges ($-\text{CO}-$) connecting ortho positions
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Analyze the electrophilic aromatic substitution: the phenolic $-\text{OH}$ group is strongly activating and ortho/para-directing via resonance delocalization of lone pair electrons.
Step 2: Protonation of formaldehyde produces the hydroxymethyl carbocation $^+\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$, which attacks the ortho and para positions of phenol to form $o$- and $p$-hydroxybenzyl alcohols.
Step 3: Under acidic conditions, the $-\text{OH}$ of the benzyl alcohol is protonated, eliminates water to generate a benzylic carbocation, which electrophilically attacks a second phenol molecule at an ortho or para position, creating a methylene bridge ($-\text{CH}_2-$).
Step 4: Therefore, the resulting linear Novolac chains consist of phenolic rings connected through methylene bridges at ortho and para positions.
Ether linkages ($-\text{CH}_2-\text{O}-\text{CH}_2-$) at meta positions are electronically disfavored because $-\text{OH}$ does not activate the meta position, and direct biphenyl $\text{C}-\text{C}$ bonds do not incorporate formaldehyde carbon.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Melamine is a symmetrical heterocyclic compound: 2,4,6-triamino-1,3,5-triazine ($\text{C}_3\text{H}_6\text{N}_6$) containing three primary exocyclic amino groups ($\text{R}-\text{NH}_2$). When heated with formaldehyde ($\text{HCHO}$) during resin manufacture, nucleophilic addition of amino nitrogens to carbonyl carbons forms methylol derivatives ($\text{R}-\text{NH}-\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$ or $\text{R}-\text{N}(\text{CH}_2\text{OH})_2$). What is the theoretical maximum number of moles of formaldehyde that can react per mole of melamine to form the completely substituted hexamethylolmelamine intermediate?
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Examine the structure of melamine: it possesses three primary amino groups ($\text{NH}_2$) attached to positions 2, 4, and 6 of the triazine ring.
Step 2: Determine reactive sites: each primary amino group has two acidic/nucleophilic hydrogen atoms bonded to nitrogen, meaning each amino group can react with up to two molecules of formaldehyde to form a bis(hydroxymethyl)amino group, $-\text{N}(\text{CH}_2\text{OH})_2$.
Step 3: Calculate the total stoichiometry: across all three amino groups, there are $3 \times 2 = 6$ reactive hydrogen atoms available for methylolation.
Step 4: Therefore, substituting into stoichiometric balance, solving yields a maximum of 6 moles of formaldehyde per mole of melamine to generate hexamethylolmelamine.
A value of 3 assumes mono-substitution at each nitrogen (trimethylolmelamine), whereas 4 or 2 corresponds to incomplete substitution.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Buna-N (nitrile rubber) is a synthetic elastomer produced by copolymerization of 1,3-butadiene ($\text{C}_4\text{H}_6$, $M = 54.09\text{ g/mol}$) and acrylonitrile ($\text{C}_3\text{H}_3\text{N}$, $M = 53.06\text{ g/mol}$). A specialized solvent-resistant grade of Buna-N undergoes quantitative elemental combustion analysis, revealing a nitrogen content of $8.40\%$ by mass. Given atomic weight $\text{N} = 14.01\text{ g/mol}$, what is the weight percentage of acrylonitrile incorporated in this copolymer?
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Calculate the theoretical mass percentage of nitrogen in pure acrylonitrile monomer: $\%\,\text{N}_{\text{AN}} = \frac{14.01}{53.06} \times 100\% = 26.40\%$.
Step 2: Since butadiene contains no nitrogen atoms, all nitrogen in the Buna-N copolymer originates exclusively from the acrylonitrile units.
Step 3: Let $w_{\text{AN}}$ be the weight fraction of acrylonitrile in the copolymer. The total nitrogen percentage is given by $\%\,\text{N}_{\text{polymer}} = w_{\text{AN}} \times \%\,\text{N}_{\text{AN}}$.
Step 4: Therefore, substituting known values, solving yields $w_{\text{AN}} = \frac{\%\,\text{N}_{\text{polymer}}}{\%\,\text{N}_{\text{AN}}} = \frac{8.40\%}{26.40\%} = 0.3182$, which corresponds to $31.8\%$ by weight.
A value of $15.9\%$ results from incorrectly using a diatomic nitrogen molecular mass ($28.02\text{ g/mol}$) in the numerator, while $42.5\%$ and $21.2\%$ result from mole fraction rather than weight fraction calculations.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Neoprene (polychloroprene) is an elastomer synthesized via free-radical emulsion polymerization of chloroprene (2-chloro-1,3-butadiene). The polymerization proceeds primarily through 1,4-addition across the conjugated diene. Which geometric isomer configuration dominates the 1,4-addition repeating units in commercial Neoprene, and what critical physical characteristic does this configuration impart to the rubber?
options: A) cis-1,4 configuration, which prevents chain alignment and reduces tensile strength
B) 1,2-addition configuration, which creates bulky chlorine side chains
C) 3,4-addition configuration, which forms a chiral syndiotactic ladder
D) trans-1,4 configuration, which promotes chain alignment and strain-induced crystallization
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Review the 1,4-addition of chloroprene: radical addition generates allylic radical intermediates that can form either trans-1,4 or cis-1,4 repeating units $-[\text{CH}_2-\text{C(Cl)}=\text{CH}-\text{CH}_2]-$.
Step 2: Analyze thermodynamic stability: due to steric hindrance between the chlorine substituent and the methylene group, the trans-1,4 configuration is significantly more stable and accounts for roughly $85-90\%$ of all repeating units in commercial Neoprene.
Step 3: Relate structure to physical properties: the regular trans-1,4 geometry permits tight chain alignment under mechanical stretching, leading to strain-induced crystallization that provides high tensile strength and tear resistance.
Step 4: Therefore, trans-1,4 configuration with strain-induced crystallization correctly describes Neoprene. Natural rubber is cis-1,4-polyisoprene, whereas Neoprene is predominantly trans-1,4.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: In the steady-state free-radical polymerization of methyl acrylate in a continuous stirred-tank reactor, the rate of chain propagation is measured to be $R_p = 4.8 \times 10^{-4}\text{ mol L}^{-1}\text{s}^{-1}$, and the rate of radical termination is measured to be $R_t = 1.2 \times 10^{-7}\text{ mol L}^{-1}\text{s}^{-1}$. At steady state, the rate of initiation equals the rate of termination ($R_i = R_t$). Calculate the kinetic chain length $\nu = \frac{R_p}{R_t}$ of this polymerization reaction, and report the value of $\frac{\nu}{1000}$ as an integer.
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Recall the definition of the kinetic chain length $
u$: it is defined as the ratio of the rate of propagation to the rate of chain initiation or termination, $
u =  rac{R_p}{R_i} =  rac{R_p}{R_t}$.
Step 2: Substitute the experimentally measured rate values: $
u =  rac{4.8 	imes 10^{-4}	ext{ mol L}^{-1}	ext{s}^{-1}}{1.2 	imes 10^{-7}	ext{ mol L}^{-1}	ext{s}^{-1}}$.
Step 3: Solving the quotient yields $
u =  rac{4.8}{1.2} 	imes 10^3 = 4 	imes 10^3 = 4000$.
Step 4: Therefore, dividing by $1000$ gives $ rac{4000}{1000} = 4$. The integer value is 4.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Nylon-2-nylon-6 is an environmentally benign, biodegradable polyamide copolymer synthesized by step-growth condensation of glycine ($\text{H}_2\text{N}-\text{CH}_2-\text{COOH}$, molar mass $75.07\text{ g/mol}$) and $\varepsilon$-aminocaproic acid ($\text{H}_2\text{N}-(\text{CH}_2)_5-\text{COOH}$, molar mass $131.17\text{ g/mol}$). If one molecule of each monomer condenses in an alternating sequence with the elimination of two water molecules ($2 \times 18.02\text{ g/mol}$), what is the formula weight of the resulting constitutional repeating unit $-[\text{NH}-\text{CH}_2-\text{CO}-\text{NH}-(\text{CH}_2)_5-\text{CO}]-$?
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Write down the chemical formulas and masses of the two condensing monomers: glycine has formula $\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{NO}_2$ ($M_1 = 75.07\text{ g/mol}$) and $\varepsilon$-aminocaproic acid has formula $\text{C}_6\text{H}_{13}\text{NO}_2$ ($M_2 = 131.17\text{ g/mol}$).
Step 2: Combine the two monomers: the total unreacted mass is $M_1 + M_2 = 75.07 + 131.17 = 206.24\text{ g/mol}$.
Step 3: Deduct the condensation byproduct: forming two amide linkages in the repeating unit eliminates two molecules of $\text{H}_2\text{O}$ ($2 \times 18.02 = 36.04\text{ g/mol}$).
Step 4: Therefore, subtracting water mass yields $M_0 = 206.24 - 36.04 = 170.20\text{ g/mol} \approx 170.2\text{ g/mol}$.
A value of $188.2\text{ g/mol}$ results from subtracting only one molecule of water ($206.2 - 18.0$), $206.2\text{ g/mol}$ subtracts zero water, and $152.2\text{ g/mol}$ erroneously subtracts three water molecules.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: In the free-radical polymerization of unsymmetrical monosubstituted vinyl monomers ($\text{CH}_2=\text{CH}-X$, such as styrene where $X = -\text{C}_6\text{H}_5$, or acrylonitrile where $X = -\text{CN}$), radical addition occurs almost exclusively in a regiospecific head-to-tail fashion. What is the fundamental electronic and steric origin of this selectivity?
options: A) Attack at $\text{CH}-X$ is favored due to polar repulsion between initiator and methylene group
B) Attack at $\text{CH}_2$ produces a more stable secondary radical stabilized by resonance/hyperconjugation and minimizes steric hindrance
C) Attack at $\text{CH}_2$ generates a primary radical that propagates significantly faster than secondary radicals
D) The carbon-substituent bond is cleaved during attack at the $\text{CH}_2$ group
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Compare the two possible sites of radical attack on the olefin $\text{CH}_2=\text{CH}-X$: attack by a radical $\text{R}\cdot$ at the less-hindered methylene carbon ($\text{CH}_2$) produces a secondary radical $\text{R}-\text{CH}_2-\dot{\text{C}}\text{H}-X$.
Step 2: Compare with the alternative: attack at the substituted methine carbon ($\text{CH}-X$) produces a primary radical $\text{R}-\text{CH}(X)-\dot{\text{C}}\text{H}_2$.
Step 3: Evaluate stability: the secondary radical $\text{R}-\text{CH}_2-\dot{\text{C}}\text{H}-X$ is strongly stabilized by resonance delocalization into the substituent $X$ (such as the phenyl $\pi$-system in styrene or nitrile $\pi$-system in acrylonitrile) and hyperconjugation. Furthermore, the unsubstituted methylene carbon is much more sterically accessible.
Step 4: Therefore, both steric and thermodynamic radical stability factors dictate head-to-tail propagation.
Attacking $\text{CH}-X$ creates a higher-energy primary radical with greater steric clash, and carbon-substituent bond cleavage does not occur in normal addition polymerization.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: During the manufacturing of low-density polyethylene (LDPE) under high-pressure free-radical conditions ($1000-3000\text{ atm}$, $200-300^\circ\text{C}$), the propagating macroradical frequently undergoes an intramolecular chain transfer known as backbiting via a cyclic six-membered transition state. What specific short-chain branch is predominantly formed along the polyethylene backbone as a direct result of this 1,5-hydrogen shift?
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Examine the geometry of the intramolecular 1,5-hydrogen shift: the growing radical end $-\text{CH}_2-\dot{\text{C}}\text{H}_2$ curls back into a strain-free six-membered ring transition state to abstract a hydrogen atom from the fifth carbon back along the chain ($-\dot{\text{C}}\text{H}_2$ abstracts $\text{H}$ from $\text{C}-5$).
Step 2: Analyze the radical product: the radical site is transferred from the chain terminus to an internal carbon atom: $-\dot{\text{C}}\text{H}-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_3$.
Step 3: Follow subsequent monomer addition: when ethylene adds to this newly created internal methine radical, chain propagation continues, leaving a dangling four-carbon pendant group: $-(\text{CH}_2)_3\text{CH}_3$, which is an $n$-butyl branch.
Step 4: Therefore, backbiting via a 1,5-hydrogen shift predominantly produces $n$-butyl branches in LDPE.
Methyl branches arise from 1,3-shifts (energetically unfavorable strained 4-membered transition states), while isopropyl or vinyl branches are not formed by standard alkane backbiting.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: In the base-catalyzed synthesis of phenol-formaldehyde resins, an excess of formaldehyde relative to phenol is employed (formaldehyde:phenol molar ratio typically between $1.5:1$ and $2.0:1$) in the presence of aqueous sodium hydroxide. The resulting prepolymer is known as a Resol. Which of the following describes the key structural features of Resol prepolymers that enable them to undergo self-crosslinking upon heating without adding any external curing agent?
options: D) Methylol groups ($-\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$) and ether linkages ($-\text{CH}_2-\text{O}-\text{CH}_2-$)
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Review the base-catalyzed condensation: the phenoxide anion attacks formaldehyde to form mono-, di-, and trimethylolphenols.
Step 2: Under alkaline conditions with excess formaldehyde, these substituted phenols condense to form low-molecular-weight prepolymers (Resols) that retain abundant reactive methylol groups ($-\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$) at open ortho and para positions, as well as some dimethylene ether bridges ($-\text{CH}_2-\text{O}-\text{CH}_2-$).
Step 3: Analyze thermal curing: upon simple heating without any additional reagent, the pendant methylol groups condense with each other and with available aromatic ring positions, eliminating water and formaldehyde to establish a dense, rigid 3D methylene-bridged Bakelite network.
Step 4: Therefore, Resol resins are uniquely characterized by reactive methylol groups and dimethylene ether linkages.
In contrast, Novolac lacks reactive methylol groups and requires hexamethylenetetramine (hexa) as a curing agent. Resols contain neither vinyl nor chloromethyl nor carboxyl functionalities.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: A vulcanized polybutadiene elastomer has an average molecular weight between cross-link junctions of $M_c = 5400\text{ g/mol}$. Given that the constitutional repeating unit of 1,4-polybutadiene is $\text{C}_4\text{H}_6$ with a formula weight of $54.0\text{ g/mol}$, calculate the average number of butadiene repeat units present in a chain segment between two successive cross-links as an integer.
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Recall the definition of the average number of repeating units between cross-links, denoted by $n_c$: it represents the ratio of the molecular weight between cross-links $M_c$ to the molecular weight of the repeat unit $M_0$.
Step 2: Calculate the repeat unit molecular weight of polybutadiene: for $\text{C}_4\text{H}_6$, $M_0 = (4 \times 12.0) + (6 \times 1.0) = 48.0 + 6.0 = 54.0\text{ g/mol}$.
Step 3: Substitute the given value of $M_c = 5400\text{ g/mol}$: $n_c = \frac{M_c}{M_0} = \frac{5400\text{ g/mol}}{54.0\text{ g/mol}} = 100$.
Step 4: Therefore, solving directly yields exactly 100 repeating units between adjacent cross-links.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Urea-formaldehyde resin is a widely utilized thermosetting polymer prepared by the reaction of urea ($\text{H}_2\text{N}-\text{CO}-\text{NH}_2$) with formaldehyde. The reaction initially produces monomethylolurea and dimethylolurea ($\text{HO}-\text{CH}_2-\text{NH}-\text{CO}-\text{NH}-\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$). Subsequent acid-catalyzed heating induces cross-linking to establish methylene bridges ($\sim\text{NH}-\text{CH}_2-\text{NH}\sim$) throughout the matrix. What small molecule byproduct is stoichiometrically eliminated during the condensation that forms these methylene bridges?
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Write down the chemical condensation step between a methylolamino group and an unreacted amino group: $\text{R}-\text{NH}-\text{CH}_2\text{OH} + \text{H}_2\text{N}-\text{R}' \to \text{R}-\text{NH}-\text{CH}_2-\text{NH}-\text{R}' + \text{H}_2\text{O}$.
Step 2: Under acid catalysis, protonation of the $-\text{OH}$ group forms a good leaving group ($-\text{OH}_2^+$), which departs as water ($\text{H}_2\text{O}$) to generate an iminium-type electrophilic carbocation ($^+\text{CH}_2-\text{NH}-\text{R}$).
Step 3: This electrophilic intermediate is attacked by a second urea nitrogen atom, releasing a proton and leaving a stable methylene bridge ($-\text{NH}-\text{CH}_2-\text{NH}-$).
Step 4: Therefore, the byproduct eliminated is water ($\text{H}_2\text{O}$).
Carbon dioxide is not formed because the carbonyl of urea remains intact; ammonia is not eliminated in this classical condensation step; and hydrogen gas is never evolved in step-growth condensations.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Polycarbonate (commercially known as Lexan) is an engineering thermoplastic prized for its optical clarity, dimensional stability, and high impact strength. It is prepared industrially by the interfacial polycondensation of Bisphenol A ($4,4'\text{-(propane-2,2-diyl)diphenol}$) with phosgene ($\text{COCl}_2$) in the presence of aqueous base. What characteristic functional group connects the Bisphenol A residues throughout the polymer chain backbone?
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Examine the functional groups of the reactants: Bisphenol A is a diphenol containing two phenolic hydroxyl groups ($\text{Ar}-\text{OH}$), while phosgene is a diacid chloride of carbonic acid ($\text{Cl}-\text{CO}-\text{Cl}$).
Step 2: Follow nucleophilic acyl substitution: in the presence of base, each phenoxide oxygen displaces a chloride ion from phosgene: $\text{Ar}-\text{O}^- + \text{Cl}-\text{CO}-\text{Cl} + ^-\text{O}-\text{Ar}' \to \text{Ar}-\text{O}-\text{CO}-\text{O}-\text{Ar}' + 2\,\text{Cl}^-$.
Step 3: Identify the resulting linkage: the ester of carbonic acid with two aryloxy groups is a carbonate ester linkage ($\sim\text{O}-\text{CO}-\text{O}\sim$).
Step 4: Therefore, the polymer is designated a polycarbonate due to the repeating carbonate linkages.
Amide linkages characterize polyamides (Nylons), carbamate linkages characterize polyurethanes, and phosphonate linkages belong to polyphosphonates.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Polyurethanes are versatile materials synthesized by the reaction of a diisocyanate (such as toluene-2,4-diisocyanate) with a diol (such as ethylene glycol). Although polyurethanes grow via a step-growth mechanism, polymer chemists classify polyurethane formation as a polyaddition reaction rather than a polycondensation reaction. What is the fundamental mechanistic reason for this distinction?
options: A) It proceeds by a free-radical chain reaction with peroxide initiator
B) It involves the elimination of $\text{CO}_2$ gas at each propagation step
C) It forms urethane linkages via hydrogen transfer without eliminating any small molecule byproduct
D) It requires ring-opening of a cyclic carbamate intermediate
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Compare polycondensation and polyaddition definitions: polycondensation involves step-growth with the stoichiometric elimination of small byproduct molecules (such as $\text{H}_2\text{O}$, $\text{HCl}$, or $\text{CH}_3\text{OH}$).
Step 2: Examine the reaction of an isocyanate with an alcohol: $\text{R}-\text{N}=\text{C}=\text{O} + \text{HO}-\text{R}' \to \text{R}-\text{NH}-\text{CO}-\text{O}-\text{R}'$.
Step 3: Observe atom economy: the nucleophilic oxygen of the alcohol attacks the electrophilic carbonyl carbon of the isocyanate, while the hydroxyl proton transfers to the adjacent isocyanate nitrogen. All atoms of both reactants are incorporated into the urethane linkage with zero byproduct loss.
Step 4: Therefore, because it proceeds by step-growth without loss of any small molecule, it is classified as a polyaddition.
It is not a radical chain reaction; evolution of $\text{CO}_2$ occurs only when water is deliberately added as a chemical blowing agent to form foams; and it does not proceed through cyclic carbamates.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: In the free-radical polymerization of vinyl monomers in the presence of a solvent $\text{S}$, the reciprocal of the number-average degree of polymerization $\frac{1}{\bar{X}_n}$ follows the classical Mayo equation: $\frac{1}{\bar{X}_n} = \frac{1}{\bar{X}_{n,0}} + C_s \frac{[\text{S}]}{[\text{M}]}$, where $[\text{S}]$ and $[\text{M}]$ are the molar concentrations of solvent and monomer, respectively. In this kinetic expression, what is the precise chemical definition of the chain transfer constant $C_s$?
options: C) The equilibrium constant for monomer coordination
D) The ratio of the rate constant of chain transfer to solvent to the propagation rate constant ($k_{tr,s}/k_p$)
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Write down the rate equations for propagation and solvent chain transfer: rate of propagation is $R_p = k_p [\text{M}][\text{P}\cdot]$, and rate of chain transfer to solvent is $R_{tr,s} = k_{tr,s} [\text{S}][\text{P}\cdot]$.
Step 2: Relate degree of polymerization to chain transfer: the fraction of chains terminated by solvent transfer relative to normal propagation is $\frac{R_{tr,s}}{R_p} = \frac{k_{tr,s} [\text{S}][\text{P}\cdot]}{k_p [\text{M}][\text{P}\cdot]} = \left(\frac{k_{tr,s}}{k_p}\right) \frac{[\text{S}]}{[\text{M}]}$.
Step 3: Define the constant $C_s$: by definition, the solvent chain transfer constant is the ratio of rate constants $C_s = \frac{k_{tr,s}}{k_p}$.
Step 4: Therefore, $C_s$ represents the ratio of the rate constant of chain transfer to solvent to the propagation rate constant ($k_{tr,s}/k_p$).
It is entirely independent of initiator dissociation efficiency, termination mode ratios, or coordination equilibria.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: An equimolar radical copolymerization of maleic anhydride (formula $\text{C}_4\text{H}_2\text{O}_3$, formula weight $98.06\text{ g/mol}$) and styrene (formula $\text{C}_8\text{H}_8$, formula weight $104.15\text{ g/mol}$) forms a strictly alternating $1:1$ copolymer due to strong electron donor-acceptor interactions. If a purified sample of this alternating copolymer has a number-average molecular weight $\bar{M}_n = 101{,}105\text{ g/mol}$, calculate the average number of styrene monomer units incorporated per polymer chain as an integer.
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Determine the molecular mass of the alternating repeat unit consisting of one maleic anhydride unit and one styrene unit: $M_0 = M_{\text{maleic}} + M_{\text{styrene}} = 98.06 + 104.15 = 202.21\text{ g/mol}$.
Step 2: Calculate the number-average degree of polymerization $\bar{X}_n$ representing the number of alternating monomer pairs: $\bar{X}_n = \frac{\bar{M}_n}{M_0} = \frac{101{,}105\text{ g/mol}}{202.21\text{ g/mol}} = 500$.
Step 3: Because the copolymer is strictly alternating with a $1:1$ stoichiometry, each repeating unit pair contains exactly one styrene monomer unit.
Step 4: Therefore, substituting into chain stoichiometry, solving yields exactly 500 styrene units per average macromolecule. The integer answer is 500.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: In the heterogeneous Ziegler-Natta polymerization of propene catalyzed by $\alpha-\text{TiCl}_3$ and $\text{Al(C}_2\text{H}_5)_3$, coordination and subsequent chain propagation follow the classical Cossee-Arlman stereoregular mechanism. What are the key elementary coordination steps and the spatial origin of the high isotacticity observed in the resulting polypropylene?
options: A) Propene coordinates through its $\pi$-system to an octahedrally vacant titanium site, followed by cis-migratory insertion into the Ti-alkyl bond with steric facial selectivity enforced by the asymmetric chloride ligand environment
B) Propene undergoes direct carbocationic attack at an axial ethyl ligand without preliminary coordination to the titanium transition metal center
C) Free-radical homolysis of the titanium-carbon bond generates a detached propyl radical that adds into propene in bulk solution
D) Propene coordinates exclusively to the aluminum center of $\text{AlEt}_3$, which undergoes concerted [2+2] cycloaddition with the titanium chloride crystal face
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Understand the active site structure: the active catalytic species consists of an octahedrally coordinated titanium center ($\text{Ti}^{3+}$) located on the crystal surface of $\alpha-\text{TiCl}_3$, possessing a Ti-alkyl (or Ti-polymer) bond and an adjacent vacant coordination site.
Step 2: Track monomer coordination: propene coordinates through its olefinic $\pi$-electrons to this vacant coordination site on titanium, forming a transition metal $\pi$-complex.
Step 3: Analyze the cis-migratory insertion: the growing polymer chain migrates to the coordinated olefin via a four-membered cyclic transition state, inserting into the olefin in a cis fashion and regenerating a vacant coordination site.
Step 4: Stereochemical control: the asymmetric steric environment of the surrounding rigid chloride crystal lattice forces propene to approach exclusively from one enantioface (re- or si-face), ensuring identical configuration at every newly generated stereocenter.
Step 5: Therefore, cis-migratory insertion into the Ti-alkyl bond governed by the chiral ligand field yields highly isotactic polypropylene. Carbocationic attack, detached radical homolysis, and exclusive coordination to aluminum do not occur in Ziegler-Natta coordination polymerization.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: A cross-linked polyester is synthesized by the step-growth condensation of trimesic acid (benzene-1,3,5-tricarboxylic acid, functionality $f_A = 3$) with 1,4-butanediol (functionality $f_B = 2$). The reaction mixture contains $2.0\text{ mol}$ of trimesic acid and $3.0\text{ mol}$ of 1,4-butanediol, providing an exact $1:1$ stoichiometric balance of carboxyl and hydroxyl groups. According to the classical Carothers gelation relationship, what is the critical fractional extent of reaction $p_c$ at which the incipient gel point is reached?
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Calculate the total initial number of monomer molecules in the system: $N_0 = N_A + N_B = 2.0\text{ mol} + 3.0\text{ mol} = 5.0\text{ mol}$.
Step 2: Calculate the total number of reactive functional groups present initially: total functional groups $= (N_A \times f_A) + (N_B \times f_B) = (2.0 \times 3) + (3.0 \times 2) = 6.0 + 6.0 = 12.0\text{ equivalents}$.
Step 3: Compute the average functionality $f_{\text{avg}}$ of the monomer mixture: $f_{\text{avg}} = \frac{\text{total functional groups}}{N_0} = \frac{12.0}{5.0} = 2.40$.
Step 4: Apply the Carothers gel point equation for multifunctional step-growth polymerization: $p_c = \frac{2}{f_{\text{avg}}}$. Substituting the average functionality yields $p_c = \frac{2}{2.40} = \frac{5}{6} \approx 0.8333$, or $83.3\%$.
Step 5: Therefore, gelation occurs at an extent of reaction $p_c = 0.833$.
A value of $0.667$ corresponds to setting $f_{\text{avg}} = 3$ without accounting for the difunctional monomer ($2/3$), $0.750$ corresponds to setting $f_{\text{avg}} = 2.67$, and $0.900$ is a typical distractor for underestimating cross-link density.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: A linear polyamide is synthesized by step-growth polymerization of adipic acid (monomer A) and hexamethylenediamine (monomer B). The initial stoichiometry has a slight excess of diamine, such that the stoichiometric ratio is $r = \frac{N_A}{N_B} = 0.980$ (where $N_A$ and $N_B$ are the initial moles of carboxyl and amino groups, respectively). If the reaction proceeds to a fractional conversion $p = 0.990$ with respect to the limiting carboxyl groups, calculate the number-average degree of polymerization $\bar{X}_n$ predicted by the Carothers equation.
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Write down the generalized Carothers equation for linear step-growth polymerization with non-stoichiometric monomer feeds: $\bar{X}_n = \frac{1 + r}{1 + r - 2rp}$, where $r = \frac{N_A}{N_B} \le 1$ is the stoichiometric ratio and $p$ is the fractional conversion of the limiting functional groups A.
Step 2: Calculate the numerator: $1 + r = 1 + 0.980 = 1.980$.
Step 3: Calculate the product in the denominator: $2rp = 2 \times 0.980 \times 0.990 = 1.960 \times 0.990 = 1.9404$.
Step 4: Compute the denominator: $1 + r - 2rp = 1.980 - 1.9404 = 0.0396$.
Step 5: Solve for the degree of polymerization: $\bar{X}_n = \frac{1.980}{0.0396} = 50.0$.
Step 6: Therefore, substituting values yields $\bar{X}_n = 50.0$.
A value of $100.0$ results from assuming an ideal $1:1$ stoichiometric ratio ($r = 1.0$), which gives $\frac{1}{1 - 0.990} = 100$. A value of $25.0$ or $75.0$ results from arithmetic errors in evaluating the denominator.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Polyacetylene ($[\text{CH}=\text{CH}]_n$) is an intrinsically conjugated organic polymer that exhibits semiconducting properties in its pristine state with an optical band gap of approximately $1.5\text{ eV}$. Upon chemical exposure to iodine vapor ($\text{I}_2$), its electrical conductivity increases by more than ten orders of magnitude into the metallic regime ($> 10^3\text{ S cm}^{-1}$). What electronic charge carriers are formed on the polyacetylene chain upon this p-type oxidative doping, and how do they mediate electrical conduction?
options: A) Mobile free electrons injected into antibonding $\sigma^*$ orbitals via n-type reduction
B) Localized carbocations that induce irreversible skeletal cleavage and cross-linking
C) Solvated electron pairs residing within interstitial micropores
D) Positively charged polarons (radical cations) and bipolarons (dications) delocalized along the conjugated $\pi$-system
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Understand the redox chemistry of doping: iodine ($\text{I}_2$) acts as a mild chemical oxidant (electron acceptor). It abstracts $\pi$-electrons from the polyacetylene chain, forming counter-anions such as triiodide ($\text{I}_3^-$) and pentaiodide ($\text{I}_5^-$).
Step 2: Identify the primary electronic defect: removal of one electron from the delocalized $\pi$-valence band creates a radical cation accompanied by local lattice relaxation (distortion of bond alternation), known as a polaron.
Step 3: Analyze higher doping levels: removal of a second electron from the chain creates a thermodynamically favorable spinless dication defect known as a bipolaron, or pair of charged solitons.
Step 4: Explain electrical transport: these positive polarons and bipolarons migrate along the conjugated polymer backbone via rapid rearrangement of alternating single and double $\pi$-bonds, producing high metallic-like electrical conductivity without breaking $\sigma$-bonds.
Step 5: Therefore, positively charged polarons and bipolarons delocalized along the conjugated $\pi$-system mediate conduction. Iodine doping is p-type (oxidative), not n-type (which requires strong reducing agents such as sodium naphthalenide).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Which of the following statements concerning the coordination polymerization of propene using heterogeneous Ziegler-Natta catalysts and the resulting polymer stereochemistry is/are scientifically CORRECT?
options: A) Heterogeneous Ziegler-Natta catalysts (such as $\alpha-\text{TiCl}_3$ combined with $\text{Al(C}_2\text{H}_5)_2\text{Cl}$) yield isotactic polypropylene where all methyl substituents possess identical relative stereochemical configurations along the backbone

B) The high stereoregularity of isotactic polypropylene permits dense crystal lattice packing, conferring high mechanical stiffness, crystallinity, and a crystalline melting point around $165-170^\circ\text{C}$

C) The Cossee-Arlman propagation mechanism involves reversible coordination of propene to an octahedral vacancy on titanium, followed by cis-migratory insertion of the coordinated olefin into the titanium-carbon bond
D) Atactic polypropylene is a highly crystalline material with a melting point exceeding that of isotactic polypropylene
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Evaluate isotactic stereochemistry: Ziegler-Natta catalyst surfaces impose rigid chiral environments that force propene insertion with consistent facial stereoselectivity, producing isotactic polypropylene where all methyl groups lie on the same side in a Fischer-type projection. Thus, statement A is correct.
Step 2: Evaluate physical properties: the uniform isotactic chain geometry easily folds into a $3_1$ helical conformation that packs into a dense crystalline lattice, yielding high crystallinity and a melting temperature of $165-170^\circ\text{C}$. Thus, statement B is correct.
Step 3: Evaluate propagation mechanism: the accepted Cossee-Arlman mechanism consists of olefin $\pi$-coordination to a vacant octahedral site on $\text{Ti}^{3+}$, followed by four-center cis-migratory insertion into the adjacent titanium-polymer $\sigma$-bond. Thus, statement C is correct.
Step 4: Evaluate atactic polypropylene: atactic polypropylene has a completely random spatial distribution of methyl groups that prevents chain packing into a crystalline lattice. Consequently, it is an amorphous, gummy, low-modulus material with no distinct crystalline melting point, refuting statement D.
Step 5: Therefore, statements A, B, and C are correct.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Consider the fundamental kinetic and mechanistic distinctions between chain-growth (addition) polymerization and step-growth (condensation) polymerization. Which of the following statements is/are scientifically CORRECT?
options: A) In step-growth polymerization, high-molecular-weight polymer chains are formed at very low conversions ($p < 0.10$) because monomer disappears almost immediately

B) In chain-growth polymerization, high-molecular-weight polymer is formed almost instantaneously upon radical initiation, while unreacted monomer remains abundant throughout the majority of the reaction

C) In the step-growth polycondensation of stoichiometric bifunctional monomers ($A-B$), achieving a high degree of polymerization ($\bar{X}_n > 100$) requires extents of reaction $p > 0.99$, as described by $\bar{X}_n = \frac{1}{1-p}$

D) Chain-growth polymerization requires an active initiation center (such as a radical, cation, anion, or coordination complex), and monomer adds exclusively to propagating active chain ends rather than reacting with other monomer molecules
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Analyze step-growth molecular weight versus conversion: in step-growth reactions, any two functional groups can react with each other (monomer with monomer, dimer with trimer, etc.). Monomer is consumed very early to form small oligomers (dimers, trimers), but high molecular weight requires nearly complete conversion ($p > 0.99$), since $\bar{X}_n = \frac{1}{1-p}$. Thus, statement A is false and statement C is correct.
Step 2: Analyze chain-growth kinetics: chain growth requires initiation to create an active center. Propagation is extremely fast relative to initiation, so each initiated chain grows to full high molecular weight within milliseconds. Unreacted monomer is consumed steadily and remains present throughout the reaction. Thus, statement B is correct.
Step 3: Analyze active center requirement: chain-growth strictly requires active centers (free radicals, cations, anions, or metal-carbon complexes) and proceeds solely by monomer addition to the active end; two unactivated monomers cannot react directly with each other. Thus, statement D is correct.
Step 4: Therefore, statements B, C, and D are correct.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Phenol-formaldehyde (Bakelite) and melamine-formaldehyde resins are premier industrial thermosetting polymers. Which of the following statements regarding their preparation, chemical structures, and curing mechanisms is/are scientifically CORRECT?
options: A) Novolac is a linear, fusible prepolymer synthesized under acid catalysis with a formaldehyde-to-phenol ratio $< 1$, which can be cured into a rigid 3D cross-linked Bakelite network by heating with hexamethylenetetramine
B) In the electrophilic aromatic substitution of phenol by formaldehyde, the phenolic $-\text{OH}$ group directs incoming electrophiles exclusively to meta positions

C) Melamine (2,4,6-triamino-1,3,5-triazine) possesses three primary amino groups that undergo methylolation with formaldehyde, facilitating extensive 3D polycondensation into scratch-resistant, unbreakable dinnerware

D) Fully cross-linked Bakelite and cured melamine-formaldehyde resins are classified as thermosets because their heavily cross-linked covalent networks cannot melt or flow upon reheating, undergoing thermal decomposition/charring instead
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Evaluate Novolac synthesis and curing: Novolac is synthesized using acid catalysts and an excess of phenol (molar ratio $\text{HCHO}:\text{phenol} < 1$). It forms linear chains connected by methylene bridges without methylol groups. Heating with hexamethylenetetramine (hexa) provides the additional methylene bridges required to cross-link into insoluble, infusible 3D Bakelite. Thus, statement A is correct.
Step 2: Evaluate electrophilic aromatic directing effects: the phenolic $-\text{OH}$ group has lone pairs that resonance-activate the ortho and para positions ($+M$ effect). Substitution occurs at ortho and para positions, not meta. Thus, statement B is false.
Step 3: Evaluate melamine-formaldehyde resin: melamine contains three primary amino groups ($-\text{NH}_2$) on a triazine ring. Reaction with formaldehyde produces methylolmelamines that condense into a rigid, non-staining, heat-resistant 3D thermoset network widely used for unbreakable melamine tableware. Thus, statement C is correct.
Step 4: Evaluate thermoset behavior: heavily cross-linked 3D networks lack thermoplastic flow mechanisms. Upon heating, covalent bonds undergo irreversible homolytic cleavage and pyrolysis rather than melting. Thus, statement D is correct.
Step 5: Therefore, statements A, C, and D are correct.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Which of the following statements regarding natural rubber, its geometric isomer gutta-percha, and synthetic elastomers is/are scientifically CORRECT?
options: A) Natural rubber is cis-1,4-polyisoprene, whose coiled conformation and weak intermolecular van der Waals forces permit high reversible elasticity upon mechanical elongation
B) Gutta-percha is trans-1,4-polyisoprene, whose regular, linear chain architecture facilitates close packing into a crystalline lattice, making it rigid and inelastic at room temperature
C) Vulcanization of natural rubber with sulfur saturates all carbon-carbon double bonds and irreversibly destroys the elasticity of the elastomer

D) Buna-N is an addition copolymer of 1,3-butadiene and acrylonitrile that exhibits exceptional resistance to the swelling and degrading action of petroleum fuels, lubricating oils, and non-polar organic solvents
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Evaluate natural rubber: natural rubber is cis-1,4-polyisoprene. The cis double bonds introduce kinks into the polymer chains, preventing tight crystalline packing. The chains adopt coiled conformations stabilized by weak van der Waals forces, enabling high elastic extensibility and recovery. Thus, statement A is correct.
Step 2: Evaluate gutta-percha: gutta-percha is the trans-1,4-stereoisomer of polyisoprene. The trans geometry provides a more linear and symmetrical backbone that readily packs into crystalline domains, producing a hard, tough, inelastic thermoplastic at room temperature. Thus, statement B is correct.
Step 3: Evaluate vulcanization chemistry: vulcanization introduces disulfide and polysulfide cross-links ($-\text{S}_x-$) between allylic carbon positions on adjacent polyisoprene chains. It does not saturate all carbon-carbon double bonds, and rather than destroying elasticity, it prevents chain slippage, significantly enhancing tensile strength and elastic recovery. Thus, statement C is false.
Step 4: Evaluate Buna-N: Buna-N (nitrile rubber) contains polar cyano groups ($-\text{CN}$) from acrylonitrile that impart high polarity, rendering the polymer insoluble and resistant to swelling in non-polar hydrocarbon fuels and oils. Thus, statement D is correct.
Step 5: Therefore, statements A, B, and D are correct.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Living anionic polymerization is an indispensable technique for the synthesis of monodisperse polymers and well-defined macromolecular architectures. Which of the following statements regarding the living anionic polymerization of styrene initiated by alkyllithium reagents (e.g. $sec-\text{C}_4\text{H}_9\text{Li}$) is/are scientifically CORRECT?
options: A) In rigorously purified aprotic non-polar solvents (such as benzene or cyclohexane), the propagating styryl carbanions undergo neither spontaneous chain termination nor chain transfer, retaining active living chain ends indefinitely

B) Sequential addition of a second distinct monomer (such as 1,3-butadiene or isoprene) to the living polystyrene carbanion solution enables the quantitative synthesis of block copolymers with narrow polydispersity

C) In an ideal living anionic polymerization where initiation is much faster than propagation, the molecular weight distribution follows a Poisson distribution, yielding a polydispersity index close to unity ($\text{PDI} \approx 1 + \frac{1}{\bar{X}_n} \to 1.0$)
D) Protic reagents such as water and ethanol act as co-catalysts that accelerate anionic chain propagation by solvating the lithium counter-cation
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Evaluate living character: in the absence of electrophilic impurities (such as moisture, air, or carbon dioxide), the carbanionic propagating centers $\sim\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}^-(\text{C}_6\text{H}_5)\text{Li}^+$ have no accessible pathways for spontaneous termination (such as $\beta$-hydride elimination) or chain transfer in aprotic solvents. Thus, statement A is correct.
Step 2: Evaluate block copolymer synthesis: because the chain ends remain active after complete consumption of the first monomer batch, adding a second conjugated diene or methacrylate monomer continues propagation from the pre-existing block, cleanly yielding well-defined diblock or triblock copolymers (such as SBS rubber). Thus, statement B is correct.
Step 3: Evaluate molecular weight distribution: rapid initiation followed by simultaneous and uniform growth of all chains produces a Poisson distribution of chain lengths, where $\text{PDI} = \frac{\bar{M}_w}{\bar{M}_n} = 1 + \frac{\bar{X}_n - 1}{\bar{X}_n^2} \approx 1 + \frac{1}{\bar{X}_n}$. For large $\bar{X}_n$, $\text{PDI} \to 1.00$ (essentially monodisperse). Thus, statement C is correct.
Step 4: Evaluate effect of protic reagents: water, alcohols, and acids act as strong chain terminators (poisons) that instantly protonate the carbanion to yield dead polymer: $\sim\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}^-(\text{C}_6\text{H}_5) + \text{H}_2\text{O} \to \sim\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_2(\text{C}_6\text{H}_5) + \text{OH}^-$. They do not act as co-catalysts. Thus, statement D is false.
Step 5: Therefore, statements A, B, and C are correct.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: In free-radical polymerization chemistry, the control of radical kinetics through inhibitors, retarders, and stable free radicals is of immense synthetic and industrial importance. Which of the following statements is/are scientifically CORRECT?
options: A) Radical inhibitors react with propagating macroradicals to form highly reactive radical species that dramatically accelerate the overall rate of monomer consumption

B) $p$-Benzoquinone acts as a potent inhibitor for styrene polymerization by adding to growing carbon radicals to form resonance-stabilized aryloxy/semiquinone radical intermediates that are unable to propagate

C) Stable nitroxide free radicals, such as 2,2,6,6-tetramethylpiperidine-1-oxyl (TEMPO), establish a reversible thermal dormant-active equilibrium with propagating radicals, providing the basis for Nitroxide-Mediated Polymerization (NMP)

D) Dissolved atmospheric oxygen ($\text{O}_2$) functions as an inhibitor in radical polymerization by reacting rapidly with carbon-centered macroradicals to form unreactive peroxy radicals ($\text{P}-\text{O}-\text{O}\cdot$)
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Understand inhibitor definition: inhibitors react with initiating or propagating radicals to convert them into stable, unreactive species that cannot add further monomer, thereby introducing an induction period during which polymerization is completely suppressed. They do not accelerate polymerization, refuting statement A.
Step 2: Mechanism of quinone inhibition: $p$-benzoquinone captures propagating carbon radicals at oxygen or the conjugated ring to form resonance-stabilized semiquinone radicals that terminate chain growth and cannot re-initiate. Thus, statement B is correct.
Step 3: Mechanism of stable nitroxide radicals: TEMPO is a persistent free radical that does not initiate polymerization, but reversibly couples with growing macroradicals to form a dormant alkoxyamine species ($\text{P}-\text{TEMPO}$). Thermal dissociation regenerates the active radical transiently, keeping the steady-state radical concentration extremely low and suppressing bimolecular termination (NMP). Thus, statement C is correct.
Step 4: Oxygen inhibition: ground-state triplet oxygen ($^3\text{O}_2$) has biradical character and reacts with propagating carbon radicals at near diffusion-controlled rates ($k \sim 10^7-10^9\text{ M}^{-1}\text{s}^{-1}$) to form resonance-stabilized peroxy radicals ($\text{P}-\text{O}-\text{O}\cdot$), which are too unreactive to add vinyl monomers, causing an induction period. Thus, statement D is correct.
Step 5: Therefore, statements B, C, and D are correct.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Biodegradable polymers are crucial materials for medical implants, drug delivery, and eco-friendly packaging. Which of the following statements regarding the synthesis, chemical linkages, and environmental degradation mechanisms of biodegradable polymers is/are scientifically CORRECT?
options: A) Poly($\beta$-hydroxybutyrate-co-$\beta$-hydroxyvalerate) (PHBV) is an aliphatic polyester that undergoes microbial degradation in natural soil via enzymatic hydrolysis of its ester linkages by bacterial depolymerases
B) Nylon-2-nylon-6 is an entirely synthetic, non-biodegradable polyamide that resists microbial cleavage due to dense intermolecular hydrogen-bonded crystalline sheets
C) Polylactic acid (PLA) is synthesized from lactic acid or cyclic lactide dimer, and undergoes hydrolytic ester cleavage in the human body to yield non-toxic, metabolizable lactic acid
D) Polyglycolic acid (PGA) possesses hydrolytically labile aliphatic ester linkages in its backbone, allowing it to be completely absorbed in vivo as dissolvable surgical sutures (Dexon)
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Evaluate PHBV biodegradability: PHBV is a bacterial polyhydroxyalkanoate (PHA) copolymer produced by microorganisms such as *Ralstonia eutropha*. Its aliphatic ester linkages are recognized and hydrolyzed by bacterial extracellular depolymerases in soil and aquatic environments, converting it to $\text{CO}_2$ and $\text{H}_2\text{O}$. Thus, statement A is correct.
Step 2: Evaluate Nylon-2-nylon-6: Nylon-2-nylon-6 is an alternating polyamide copolymer of glycine and $\varepsilon$-aminocaproic acid. Unlike Nylon 6 or Nylon 6,6, Nylon-2-nylon-6 was deliberately engineered as a biodegradable polyamide whose peptide-like amide bonds are susceptible to microbial enzymes. Thus, statement B is false.
Step 3: Evaluate PLA synthesis and degradation: polylactic acid is prepared by ring-opening polymerization of lactide. In aqueous physiological environments, it undergoes spontaneous non-enzymatic hydrolytic ester cleavage to monomeric lactic acid, which enters the Krebs cycle and is eliminated as $\text{CO}_2$ and $\text{H}_2\text{O}$. Thus, statement C is correct.
Step 4: Evaluate PGA suture chemistry: polyglycolic acid is an aliphatic polyester with high hydrolytic sensitivity. In bodily tissues, it undergoes ester hydrolysis to glycolic acid over several weeks, making it the premier material for absorbable surgical sutures. Thus, statement D is correct.
Step 5: Therefore, statements A, C, and D are correct.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Stereochemical tacticity exerts a profound influence on the morphology, crystalline melting point, and mechanical performance of vinyl polymers $-[\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}(R)]_n-$. Which of the following statements regarding polymer tacticity is/are scientifically CORRECT?
options: A) In an isotactic polymer, all pseudo-asymmetric carbon centers have identical stereochemical configuration, so all pendant substituents $R$ lie on the same face of the plane when drawn in an extended all-trans zigzag projection

B) In a syndiotactic polymer, the pseudo-asymmetric centers alternate configurations regularly along the chain, so that the pendant substituents $R$ alternate systematically from one face to the opposite face in an all-trans planar projection
C) Atactic polymers have completely identical stereochemical configurations at every repeat unit, which maximizes three-dimensional crystal lattice formation and elevates the melting point

D) Syndiotactic polystyrene can be synthesized using single-site metallocene catalysts (such as $\text{CpTiCl}_3$ activated by methylaluminoxane) and exhibits a high crystalline melting point of approximately $270^\circ\text{C}$
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Define isotactic stereochemistry: an isotactic polymer has identical stereocenter configurations ($R, R, R...$ or $S, S, S...$) at every substituted carbon, placing all pendant $R$ groups on the same side of the chain in an extended all-trans zigzag conformation. Thus, statement A is correct.
Step 2: Define syndiotactic stereochemistry: a syndiotactic polymer alternates stereocenter configurations systematically ($R, S, R, S...$), placing pendant $R$ groups on alternating sides of the planar zigzag backbone. Thus, statement B is correct.
Step 3: Analyze atactic polymer properties: atactic polymers have random stereocenter configurations. This structural irregularity prevents chains from packing into an ordered crystalline lattice, rendering atactic polymers completely amorphous with low glass transition temperatures and no melting point. Statement C erroneously attributes this to atactic polymers. Thus, statement C is false.
Step 4: Evaluate syndiotactic polystyrene: metallocene catalysis enables the synthesis of syndiotactic polystyrene (sPS), whose high stereochemical regularity allows it to crystallize readily, yielding a semi-crystalline engineering thermoplastic with a high melting temperature of $270^\circ\text{C}$. Thus, statement D is correct.
